requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: During a TLS negotiation, an email client (i.e., an SMTP, IMAP, POP3, or ManageSieve client) MUST check its understanding of the server identity (client's reference identifiers) against the server's identity as presented in the server Certificate message in order to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: For DNS-ID and CN-ID identifier types, the client MUST use one or more of the following as "reference identifiers": (a) the domain portion of the user's email address, (b) the hostname it used to open the connection (without CNAME canonicalization).

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: The client MAY also use (c) a value securely derived from (a) or (b), such as using "secure" DNSSEC [RFC4033] [RFC4034] [RFC4035] validated lookup.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: When using email service discovery procedure specified in [RFC6186], the client MUST also use the domain portion of the user's email address as another "reference identifier" to compare against an SRV-ID identifier in the server certificate.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: Support for the DNS-ID identifier type (subjectAltName of dNSName type [RFC5280]) is REQUIRED in email client software implementations.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: Support for the SRV-ID identifier type (subjectAltName of SRVName type [RFC4985]) is REQUIRED for email client software implementations that support [RFC6186].

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: A URI-ID identifier type (subjectAltName of uniformResourceIdentifier type [RFC5280]) MUST NOT be used by clients for server verification, as URI-IDs were not historically used for email.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: For backward compatibility with deployed software, a CN-ID identifier type (CN attribute from the subject name, see [RFC6125]) MAY be used for server identity verification.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: The "*" wildcard character MAY be used as the left-most name component of a DNS-ID or CN-ID in the certificate.

requirements.heading: Email Server Certificate Verification Rules
requirements.text: Note that the wildcard character MUST NOT be used as a fragment of the left-most name component (e.g., "*oo.example.com", "f*o.example.com", or "foo*.example.com").

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Certification Authorities
requirements.text: CAs MUST support issuance of server certificates with a DNS-ID identifier type (subjectAltName of dNSName type [RFC5280]).

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Certification Authorities
requirements.text: CAs MUST support issuance of server certificates with an SRV-ID identifier type (subjectAltName of SRVName type [RFC4985]) for each type of email service.

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Certification Authorities
requirements.text: For backward compatibility with a deployed client base, CAs MUST support issuance of server certificates with a CN-ID identifier type (CN attribute from the subject name, see [RFC6125]).

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Certification Authorities
requirements.text: CAs MAY allow "*" (wildcard) as the left-most name component of a DNS-ID or CN-ID in server certificates it issues.

requirements.heading: Notes on Handling of Delegated Email Services by Certification
requirements.text: In particular, CAs that can't verify such authorization (whether for a particular domain or in general) MUST NOT include such email SRV-IDs/DNS-IDs in certificates they issue.

requirements.heading: Notes on Handling of Delegated Email Services by Certification
requirements.text: A CA willing to sign a certificate containing a particular DNS-ID SHOULD also support signing a certificate containing one or more of the email SRV-IDs for the same domain because the SRV-ID effectively provides more restricted access to an email service for the domain (as opposed to unrestricted use of any services for the same domain, as specified by the DNS-ID).

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Mail Service Providers and Certificate
requirements.text: MUST include the DNS-ID identifier type in Certificate Signing Requests for the host name(s) where the email server(s) are running.

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Mail Service Providers and Certificate
requirements.text: They SHOULD include the DNS-ID identifier type in Certificate Signing Requests for the domain portion of served email addresses.

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Mail Service Providers and Certificate
requirements.text: MUST include the SRV-ID identifier type for each type of email service in Certificate Signing Requests if the email services provided are discoverable using DNS SRV as specified in [RFC6186].

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Mail Service Providers and Certificate
requirements.text: SHOULD include the CN-ID identifier type for the host name where the email server(s) is running in Certificate Signing Requests for backward compatibility with deployed email clients.

requirements.heading: Compliance Checklist for Mail Service Providers and Certificate
requirements.text: MAY include "*" (wildcard) as the left-most name component of a DNS-ID or CN-ID in Certificate Signing Requests.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: When the reference identity is an IP address, the iPAddress subjectAltName SHOULD be used by the client for comparison.
